parameters.question: Compare top 10 most important genes (by absolute logistic regression coefficient) from a cancer vs. normal classifier trained on a 70/30 split. At least 7 of 10 genes must overlap with the reference set (ranks near 10 are solver-sensitive); coefficient values for overlapping genes must be within +/-0.05; column naming and ordering may differ.

files.strategy_reasoning: The 70/30 split makes the task stochastic, but the output is a small 10-row table, so it should be checked value by value rather than by distribution. Approximate matching can align the gene records, test the 7-of-10 overlap and apply the ±0.05 coefficient tolerance even when column names or order differ.

align_plan.reasoning: Both tables have the same layout (genes as rows), so no transpose is needed. The reference columns Gene and Coefficient match candidate columns with the same names. The candidate's extra Rank and AbsCoefficient columns are derived values with no counterpart in the reference, so they are left out. Rows are matched on Gene, a categorical identifier. Coefficient is a computed value, so it is not used as a key. The guideline scores how many genes overlap (at least 7 of 10) and allows rank differences near position 10, so row order is treated as not mattering and the comparison checks the gene set as a permutation.

column_configs.name: Coefficient
column_configs.reasoning: The guideline allows an absolute difference of ±0.05 between coefficients. With values around 0.17–0.20, a relative absolute error of 0.25 matches ±0.05 at the top of the range and is slightly stricter for smaller values. The sign is kept because the direction of a coefficient matters.

comparison_plan.overall_reasoning: The rows are aligned on Gene, so the gene-overlap requirement (at least 7 of 10 genes) is handled by alignment on the ID column. The only reference data column is Coefficient. The guideline allows an absolute difference of ±0.05 in coefficient values. The coefficients range from about 0.17 to 0.20, so a relative absolute error of 0.25 matches ±0.05 at the largest value (0.05/0.20 = 0.25) and is slightly stricter for the smaller ones. Sign is kept (compare_abs=false) because a coefficient's sign shows whether a gene points toward cancer or normal tissue. The candidate's extra columns (Rank, AbsCoefficient) are not in the reference, so they are not compared.
